policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וָאַרְבֶּה and ketiv וארב are the same hiphil consecutive of רבה, differing only in plene vs. defective final he; both yield 'and multiplied'. ASV 'and multiplied his seed' renders the verb without any feature that separates the two spellings, and there is no ASV note at JOS.24.3. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

Qere וָאָבִיְא and ketiv ואבאה are orthographic variants of the same hiphil consecutive of בוא, 'and I brought'. ASV 'And I brought you into the land of the Amorites' matches either spelling identically, and JOS.24.8 carries no textual note. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.

Qere מֵעֵבר ('from beyond') and ketiv בעבר ('in the region beyond') both describe the same trans-Euphrates location, and ASV renders each construction alike as 'beyond the River' (cf. 'beyond the Jordan' in 24:8 with no 'from'). ASV 'that were beyond the River' therefore does not distinguish the preposition, and JOS.24.15 has no textual note. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
